display.text: The overall test of H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = … = μ_k against the alternative that not all population means are equal. Rejection establishes at least one difference without identifying which pairs differ.
Assuming equal population means and the model conditions, the probability of an F statistic at least as large as the observed one.
Variation among group sample means, assessed relative to within-group variation to determine whether observed mean differences exceed those expected from sampling alone.

The classical ANOVA assumption that response variability is the same across populations. The text checks whether the largest sample SD is less than twice the smallest as a rough diagnostic. Also called homogeneity of variance.
An ANOVA effect-size measure giving the share of total response variation associated with the group factor: between-group SS divided by total SS in one-way ANOVA. Notation: η².
A nonnegative reference distribution indexed by numerator and denominator degrees of freedom; ANOVA uses its right tail to assess the observed F statistic under equal population means.
In one-way ANOVA, the ratio of between-group mean square to within-group mean square. Large values indicate greater separation among group means relative to within-group variability.
An interval estimating one group's population mean. Comparing such intervals can aid exploration, but their overlap is not a formal test of the difference between two means.
An ANOVA sum of squares divided by its associated degrees of freedom; the between-group and error mean squares form the F ratio. Abbreviated MS.
Follow-up comparisons used to identify particular group mean differences after an overall ANOVA, with procedures that account for testing multiple comparisons. Also called post hoc comparisons.

A method comparing population means of a quantitative response across independent groups defined by one categorical explanatory variable, by comparing variation between and within groups. Abbreviated ANOVA.
A design with more than two linked measurements or conditions on the same subjects; introduced as the dependent-samples extension beyond the independent-groups ANOVA taught here.
A measure of variation formed by adding squared deviations. The ANOVA output partitions total SS into between-group SS and within-group (error) SS.
Tukey's honestly significant difference procedure for comparing pairs of group means while controlling the family of pairwise comparisons.
Variation of individual responses around their own group means, providing the background variability against which between-group differences are assessed.
